title: GPT 5.5 biosafety bounty
description: OpenAI announced a biosafety bounty for GPT 5.5, offering rewards for identifying potential safety issues in biological applications of the model. Hacker News discussion highlights community concerns about AI safety.
author: OpenAI (discussed on Hacker News)

title: Show HN: A Karpathy-style LLM wiki your agents maintain
description: GitHub project showcasing a Karpathy-style LLM wiki that AI agents maintain automatically using Markdown and Git, demonstrating agentic systems that can self-document and update knowledge bases.
author: nex-crm (discussed on Hacker News)

title: Open source memory layer so any AI agent can do what Claude.ai and ChatGPT do
description: Open source project implementing a memory layer for AI agents, providing persistent memory capabilities similar to Claude.ai and ChatGPT. Discussion on Hacker News explores approaches to agent memory.
author: alash3al (discussed on Hacker News)

title: Lambda Calculus Benchmark for AI
description: Project proposing Lambda Calculus as a benchmark for AI reasoning capabilities, discussed on Hacker News as a way to test fundamental computational reasoning in language models.
author: victortaelin (discussed on Hacker News)

title: Google plans to invest up to $40B in Anthropic
description: Bloomberg report discussing Google's planned $40B investment in Anthropic, highlighting the intensifying AI arms race and big tech's bet on Anthropic as an AI leader. Extensive Hacker News discussion.
author: Bloomberg (discussed on Hacker News)

title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released V4 series preview models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Simon Willison analyzes their performance and pricing positioning as near-frontier models at significantly lower costs than Western competitors.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Code quality postmortem: agentic systems are fragile
description: Anthropic published a postmortem on Claude Code quality issues. Three separate harness bugs (not model issues) caused problems, including a bug that cleared thinking context every turn instead of once. Simon highlights the complexity of building agentic systems.
author: Simon Willison

title: Honker: Postgres NOTIFY/LISTEN semantics for SQLite
description: A Rust SQLite extension implementing transactional outbox pattern for SQLite, enabling queue and stream semantics with NOTIFY/LISTEN-style functionality. Uses WAL mode polling for near-real-time updates.
author: Simon Willison

title: Bluesky's For You feed: 72K users on a gaming PC
description: spacecowboy's Bluesky For You feed serves 72,000 users from a single Go process on a gaming PC (16 cores, 96GB RAM, 4TB NVMe) with SQLite storing 90 days of data (419GB). Total cost: $30/month. Could theoretically scale to all 1M Bluesky users.
author: Simon Willison (citing spacecowboy)

title: Tool Attention Is All You Need: Dynamic Tool Gating for Agentic Workflows
description: Paper proposing 'Tool Attention' mechanism with dynamic tool gating and lazy schema loading to eliminate the MCP/tools tax in scalable agentic workflows, addressing performance overhead in tool-using AI agents.
author: Anuj Sadani, Deepak Kumar

title: From Research Question to Scientific Workflow: Agentic AI for Science Automation
description: Paper exploring leveraging agentic AI to automate scientific workflows from research question to execution, potentially transforming how scientists conduct research by automating complex multi-step processes.
author: Bartosz Balis, Michal Orzechowski, Piotr Kica, Michal Dygas, Michal Kuszewski

title: Separable Expert Architecture: Privacy-Preserving LLM Personalization
description: Paper proposing a separable expert architecture for privacy-preserving LLM personalization via composable adapters and deletable user proxies, addressing privacy concerns in personalized AI systems.
author: Chris Schneider, Philipp Schoenegger, Ben Bariach

title: Thinking with Reasoning Skills: Fewer Tokens, More Accuracy
description: Paper proposing methods to achieve higher accuracy with fewer tokens by focusing on reasoning skills, suggesting efficiency improvements in LLM inference for ACL 2026 Industry Track.
author: Guangxiang Zhao, Qilong Shi, Xusen Xiao, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang, Lin Sun

title: GPT-5.5 available in OpenAI Codex
description: GPT-5.5 is out, available in OpenAI Codex and rolling out to paid ChatGPT subscribers. Simon found it fast, effective and highly capable—'I ask it to build things and it builds exactly what I ask for.'
author: Simon Willison

title: LiteParse for the web: PDF text extraction in browser
description: Simon ported LlamaIndex's LiteParse PDF extraction to run entirely in the browser using the same libraries as the Node.js version, enabling client-side PDF text extraction without server.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in a 27B Dense Model
description: Qwen released a 27B dense model claiming flagship-level agentic coding performance, surpassing their previous 397B MoE model. Simon tested the quantized version (16.8GB) locally with excellent results on SVG generation tasks, achieving 25 tokens/sec generation speed.
author: Simon Willison

title: GitHub Copilot pricing changes reflect agentic compute demands
description: GitHub changed Copilot Individual plans: tightening usage limits, pausing signups, restricting Opus 4.7 to Pro+ plan. Simon notes that agentic workflows fundamentally changed compute demands—long-running parallelized sessions consume far more resources than original plan structures supported.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox 150: Claude Mythos Preview found 271 vulnerabilities
description: Mozilla applied Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox and found/fixed 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox 150. CTO Bobby Holley: 'Defenders finally have a chance to win, decisively.' Shows AI's potential for security work.
author: Simon Willison (citing Bobby Holley)

title: Claude Code $100/month pricing confusion
description: Anthropic quietly updated pricing page to show $100/month plan, then reverted. Simon analyzes the confusion around Claude Code pricing and compares to GitHub Copilot's recent pricing changes.
author: Simon Willison

title: ChatGPT Images 2.0: GPT-3 to GPT-5 level leap
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.0. Sam Altman claimed the leap from gpt-image-1 to gpt-image-2 is equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Simon tested it with image generation prompts.
author: Simon Willison

title: Less human AI agents, please
description: Andreas Påhlsson-Notini argues current AI agents are too human in the wrong ways—lacking stringency, patience, focus. They drift toward familiar tasks and negotiate with constraints instead of executing reliably.
author: Andreas Påhlsson-Notini (via Simon Willison)

title: Claude Opus 4.7 tokenizer increases token counts by 1.46x
description: Simon built a token counter comparison tool and found Opus 4.7's new tokenizer uses 1.46x more tokens than 4.6 for the same text. For high-res images, the increase is 3x (but only due to supporting higher resolutions). This means effective 40% price increase despite same per-token pricing.
author: Simon Willison

title: Headless everything for personal AI
description: Matt Webb and Marc Benioff predict headless services will become common as personal AIs interact via APIs rather than GUIs. Salesforce Headless 360 exposes everything as API/MCP/CLI. This could disrupt per-head SaaS pricing.
author: Simon Willison (citing Matt Webb, Marc Benioff)
